question: A vendor sells oranges at ₹29 each and incurs a loss of 75%. If he wants to make a profit of 75%, at what price (in ₹) should he sell each orange?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Selling Price** in two cases: SP₁ : SP₂ = (100 − Loss%) : (100 + Profit%).

Given: SP₁ = 29, Loss₁ = 75%, Profit₂ = 75%.

Ratio = (100 − 75) : (100 + 75) = 25 : 175 = 1 : 7.

Since 1 unit represents ₹29, then 7 units represent 7 × 29 = ₹203.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹203.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial **Selling Price (SP₁)** = ₹29, **Loss Percentage** = 75%, Target **Profit Percentage** = 75%.

**Formulas:** CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Loss%) | SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5cd945f28d43297ca10519fc1d2fc934c372f34d97bce8b0c43a110ae6c38305.png] 

⇒ First, find **Cost Price (CP)**: CP = 29 × 100 ÷ (100 − 75) = 29 × 100 ÷ 25

⇒ CP = 29 × 4 = ₹116

⇒ Now, find New **Selling Price (SP₂)** for 75% profit: SP₂ = 116 × (100 + 75) ÷ 100

⇒ SP₂ = 116 × 175 ÷ 100 = 116 × (7 ÷ 4)

⇒ SP₂ = 29 × 7 = ₹203

**∴ The correct answer is ₹203.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price and Selling Price

**Cost Price (CP)** is the price at which an item is bought. **Selling Price (SP)** is the price at which it is sold. If SP > CP, it is a **Profit**; if CP > SP, it is a **Loss**.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Note that these are always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise.
